label: Buša

names.text: "Busha" and "Busa" from the Wikipedia article's alternative-names line; "Busa" is the unaccented form of the label.

about.text: A small, short-horned traditional cattle breed, or group of breeds, of south-eastern Europe, principally in Albania and the countries of the former Yugoslavia. The cattle are used as draught animals and for beef and milk. Yield is generally 600 to 1,500 kg a year, varying by region.

sources.text: Wikipedia article: "a breed or group of breeds of small short-horned cattle"; distributed in south-eastern Europe, principally in Albania and the former Yugoslavia; "used as draught animals, and for beef and milk production"; yield "generally in the range 600–1500 kg" per year, varying by region.

origin.place: South-eastern Europe, principally Albania and the countries of the former Yugoslavia (Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia).

sources.text: Wikipedia article: origin and distribution list Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. The article gives no date of formation, only that it is "a traditional breed or group of breeds". The regions field takes the first four countries in the article's order (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia), so Kosovo and North Macedonia are not listed.
Wikipedia article, citing DAD-IS breed data sheets: Albania (2014) 760 cows and 67 bulls. The total of 827 is worked out as 760 + 67.
Wikipedia article, citing DAD-IS breed data sheets: Croatia (2013) 785 animals, including 385 cows and 35 bulls.
Wikipedia article, citing DAD-IS breed data sheets: Serbia (2013) 700.
Wikipedia article, citing DAD-IS breed data sheets: Montenegro (2013) 150.
Wikipedia article, citing DAD-IS breed data sheets: Bosnia and Herzegovina (2013) 80 animals, including 70 cows.
Wikipedia article: "used as draught animals, and for beef and milk production". Listed in the article's order.

Wikipedia article: FAO (2007) lists the breed as "not at risk". The article's country listings are mixed: Croatia, Montenegro and Serbia are listed as at risk, while Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia are unknown. The DAD-IS record itself was not opened.

facts.v: Until the mid-20th century it was the dominant cattle breed across much of the Balkans.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, on the breed's history.

facts.v: Y-chromosome data link the breed to Simmental and Italian cattle, and to Red Gorbatov and Yurino cattle of Central Asia.
In the early 20th century, Croatian Buša were crossbred with Austrian Montafon and Tyrolean Grey bulls.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, on the history of Croatian cattle.

facts.v: Heifers reach sexual maturity at about two years. Fertility is reported at 85 to 90 per cent, and lifespan at about twenty years.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, on the breed's traits.

gaps: No per-lactation yield or lactation length found (the article gives only the 600 to 1,500 kg a year range). The yield range is not attributed to a country, and no year is given for it. No formation date. The North Macedonia figure is a range (1,000 to 2,000) so it is left out of head. Kosovo has no population figure. The DAD-IS records themselves were not opened (the DAD-IS URL returned 404); the population and risk figures come from the Wikipedia article, which cites DAD-IS.
